text.p: Reebok International Ltd's chief of promoting the firm's brand image said he was unhappy with the firm's advertising efforts.

Reebok outfitted more than 3,000 athletes at the Olympics and raised its advertising budget during the year. But, "as it turned out, our advertising did not successfully deliver our brand essence and it failed to connect with our target customer," Bob Meers said in a conference call.
The Olympics established the footwear company in the United States as a broad-based sports brand and portrayed its worldwide reach, said Meers, a Reebok executive vice president.
But the Atlanta Games "did not translate into retail sell-through as much as we would have liked," he said.
However, the Olympics resulted in strong retail sales, both in footwear and apparel, on the international market, particularly in Asia Pacific, most of Latin America and Northern Europe, he said.
